messages:
jordan.m: FYI customer (acct: acme-payments) reports a p99 latency regression on halcyon-1b for long contexts after yesterday's tokenizer patch. p95 ~300ms -> 800ms, p99 ~2.1s -> 5.8s. Sample request ids: req-20260315-4451, req-20260315-4459. Repro below.

jordan.m: Repro (curl):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model": "halcyon-1b", "input": "A. " + "lorem ipsum " * 9000, "max_tokens": 512, "stream": false}'
```

lee.eng: Thanks — is this limited to halcyon-1b or does halcyon-2/3 show it too? Any schema/auth differences?

priya_oncall: Pager fired at 2026-03-15T11:37:02Z for support:p99-surge-halcyon-1b. I'm collecting SLO graphs now.

sre-bot: [alert] support:p99-surge-halcyon-1b triggered (threshold 4s). Current p99=5.8s, p95=820ms. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/alert-7312

matt-ml: Noted. We shipped a tokenizer merge (bpe-merge v3) yesterday that changed split boundaries for long runs. Hypothesis: increased tokenization granularity causing larger KV cache fragmentation and more cache misses for long-context generation.

lee.eng: Can you attach a small reproducer using the SDK? Also include the `x-request-id` header from the failing requests if available.

jordan.m: Repro (python, SDK):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
prompt = "Repeat: " + "word " * 20000
resp = client.generate(model="halcyon-1b", input=prompt, max_tokens=256, debug_trace=True)
print(resp.latency_ms, resp.request_id)
```
Headers from customer: x-request-id: req-20260315-4451, req-20260315-4459.

matt-ml: Good. Two immediate checks: 1) compare token counts on old vs new tokenizer for the same prompt (`len(tokenizer.encode(p))`). 2) check KV cache hit ratio per request id. I suspect the new merge produces fewer, larger tokens causing different attention patterns and increased decode time for long sequences.

lee.eng: I ran the repro locally against staging-halcyon-1b with bpe-v3 and saw p99 ~4.9s, consistent. With bpe-v2 (pre-patch) p99 ~1.9s. So the tokenizer change correlates.

priya_oncall: Mitigations we can do right away:
- pin affected customers to model variant `halcyon-1b@tok-v2` (older tokenizer)
- enable `prefix_kv_cache=true` on routes for halcyon-1b to reduce re-computation
- temporarily lower concurrency/batching for long-context routes to avoid queuing tail latency spikes

lee.eng: I can open a rollback canary to `halcyon-1b@tok-v2` for the affected tenant and route traffic over the next 30m. Priya — can you confirm SLA implications?

priya_oncall: Confirmed — canary is fine for short window. Rollback will reduce p99 for those requests and keep overall capacity stable. I'm creating a support ticket to notify customer.

matt-ml: Longer term: revert tokenizer merge or adjust the merge parameters. We should run a token-distribution sweep on our long-context corpora and re-evaluate kernel selection heuristics that trigger during large-token decode. Also add automated perf gates for tokenizer variants during onboarding.

lee.eng: Action items:
- jordan.m: collect 10 full request traces (headers + debug_trace) and drop into the incident thread.
- priya_oncall: start the canary rollback to tok-v2 for acme-payments and notify customer.
- matt-ml: patch ML repo with token-distribution analysis and proposed merge parameter adjustments.
- lee.eng: monitor p95/p99 for 60m and escalate if no improvement.

jordan.m: Uploaded traces here: https://files.redwood.ai/incident/1711502468/traces.zip (includes req ids).

sre-bot: [deploy] started canary rollback halcyon-1b -> halcyon-1b@tok-v2 (canary id: cb-331).

priya_oncall: Canary results after 12m: p99 for acme-payments dropped from 5.8s -> 1.8s. Marking as mitigation success. Will keep canary live for 30m then decide on full rollback vs toggle per-customer routing.

matt-ml: Thanks. I'll schedule an immediate follow-up with eng-ml to either revert the merge or tune it and add perf tests.

lee.eng: Closing loop: customer notified, canary successful. Keeping this thread open for the permanent fix. Add any new traces here. :thumbsup:
